title: Formal Jacobian minors detect a nondegenerate binary quadratic hypersurface
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge2$, $T=F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak n=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)$, and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subseteq\mathfrak n$. Set $R=T/I$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n/I$. Let $J\subseteq R$ be the ideal generated by the images of the $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ minors [def-weil-matrix, def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] of the matrix $(\partial f_j/\partial t_i)$, where formal differentiation is termwise differentiation of power series. Then the following are equivalent: (a) $\operatorname{depth}(R)=1$ [def-weil-pbc-depth] and $J=\mathfrak m$; (b) $R$ is isomorphic as a complete local $F$-algebra to $F[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for some $a,b,c\in F$ with $b^2-4ac\ne0$. (c) $R$ is isomorphic as a ring (not necessarily $F$-linearly) to $F[[u,v]]/(au^2+buv+cv^2)$ for some $a,b,c\in F$ with $b^2-4ac\ne0$. The discriminant condition means that the linear map with matrix $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}2a&b\\ b&2c\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is invertible, including in characteristic $2$.

source.place: Tags 0C4C (lemma-fitting-ideal), equivalence (1) and (3), and 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), conditions (1) and (3); condition (1) of 0C49 (reduced, embedding dimension 2, a nondegenerate quadric in Sym^2 of the cotangent space vanishing in m^2/m^3) is invariant under ring isomorphisms, the residue-field isomorphism transporting the quadric, which gives (c) to (b). n>=2 avoids the negative-minor convention.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-formal-minimal-presentation-minors] to obtain $R\cong S/H$ with $H\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$, cotangent dimension $e$, and the residual ideal $D$ identified with $J$. This reduction uses only the original presentation and applies in both directions below.

source.place: 0C4C, minimal-coordinate elimination and Jacobian block calculation.

proof.text: Assume (a). Depth is unchanged by this ring isomorphism, since it identifies maximal ideals and regular sequences. Thus $\operatorname{depth}(S/H)=1$ and $D=\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-trf-minimal-jacobian-binary-hypersurface] to obtain $e=2$, $H=(f)$ with $f\ne0$, and $f_2=au^2+buv+cv^2$ with $b^2-4ac\ne0$.

source.place: 0C4C, depth-one minimal hypersurface and quadratic discriminant.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-formal-binary-morse] to $f$. The automorphism sending $f$ to $f_2$ induces $S/(f)\cong F[[u,v]]/(f_2)$ as an $F$-algebra. These local isomorphisms preserve maximal ideals and all their powers, hence are continuous with continuous inverses for the adic topologies. This gives (b). Forgetting structure gives (c).

Conversely assume (c), with model $M=F[[u,v]]/(Q)$. The discriminant condition implies $Q\ne0$, so [lem-trf-binary-quadratic-model-depth] gives depth $M=1$. The given ring isomorphism identifies regular sequences, yielding depth $R=1$. By [lem-trf-cotangent-quadratic-relation-invariance], the cotangent dimension of the model, and hence $e$, is $2$. Therefore $S=F[[z_1,z_2]]$ is regular local of dimension $2$ by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete]. Apply [lem-trf-regular-surface-depth-one-principal] to $H\subseteq\mathfrak p^2\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and depth $S/H=1$: $H=(f)$ for some nonzero $f\in\mathfrak p^2$.

source.place: 0C49, model depth and cotangent dimension; 0C48(2), principal kernel.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-cotangent-quadratic-relation-invariance], the model has quadratic-relation space $FQ$, and the abstract ring isomorphism carries its nondegenerate relation to a nondegenerate relation of $S/(f)$. The latter relation space is $Ff_2$ by the same node. Hence $f_2=az_1^2+bz_1z_2+cz_2^2$ has $b^2-4ac\ne0$: nonzero scalar rescaling multiplies the polar determinant by its square. The linear parts of $f_{z_1},f_{z_2}$ are $2az_1+bz_2,bz_1+2cz_2$, so they form a basis modulo $\mathfrak m^2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] they generate $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-minor-invariance] these derivatives generate the same residual $D$ as the original $h_j$. Step 1 identifies $D$ with $J$, proving (a).

source.place: 0C49, semilinear quadratic relation; 0C4C and 0C4B, gradient and minors.

proof_origin.place: Tags 0C4C, 0C48 and 0C49; short assembly of the four extracted statement-only arguments and the existing binary Morse lemma. The semilinear invariance supplement follows the intrinsic condition in 0C49.

lean.statement: theorem formal_jacobian_quadratic_criterion (F : Type u) [Field F] (n s : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (I : Ideal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F)) (hI : I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F)) (f : Fin s → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (hgen : I = Ideal.span (Set.range f)) : ((Ideal.depth (formalJacobianMaximalIdeal F n I) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F ⧸ I) = (1 : ℕ∞) ∧ formalJacobianIdeal F n s I f = formalJacobianMaximalIdeal F n I) ↔ ∃ (a b c : F), b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c ≠ 0 ∧ Nonempty ((MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F ⧸ I) ≃ₐ[F] (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F ⧸ Ideal.span ({MvPowerSeries.C a * (MvPowerSeries.X 0) ^ 2 + MvPowerSeries.C b * (MvPowerSeries.X 0 * MvPowerSeries.X 1) + MvPowerSeries.C c * (MvPowerSeries.X 1) ^ 2} : Set (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F))))) ∧ ((∃ (a b c : F), b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c ≠ 0 ∧ Nonempty ((MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F ⧸ I) ≃ₐ[F] (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F ⧸ Ideal.span ({MvPowerSeries.C a * (MvPowerSeries.X 0) ^ 2 + MvPowerSeries.C b * (MvPowerSeries.X 0 * MvPowerSeries.X 1) + MvPowerSeries.C c * (MvPowerSeries.X 1) ^ 2} : Set (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F))))) ↔ ∃ (a b c : F), b ^ 2 - 4 * a * c ≠ 0 ∧ Nonempty ((MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F ⧸ I) ≃+* (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F ⧸ Ideal.span ({MvPowerSeries.C a * (MvPowerSeries.X 0) ^ 2 + MvPowerSeries.C b * (MvPowerSeries.X 0 * MvPowerSeries.X 1) + MvPowerSeries.C c * (MvPowerSeries.X 1) ^ 2} : Set (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) F)))))
